name: Executive order of November 26, 1884 setting apart the Tongue River (Northern Cheyenne) Reservation
promises: Royce records that the order set apart a reservation for the Northern Cheyennes along the Rosebud River in Montana, excluding tracts located, resided on and improved by settlers before October 1, 1884.
today: The order created a reservation and took no land; no finding about it was located.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 918

openQuestions: treaties.json also lists the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma; this order concerned the Northern Cheyenne only.
The exclusion of settlers' tracts inside the boundaries, and the Northern Cheyenne Commission dockets (329), were not followed up.
The Northern Cheyenne Tribe's own account of the 1884 order was not located.
